# Phantom: CHIP-8 emulator in Rust

> A CHIP-8 emulator in Rust by Pavan Nallamothu where the CPU is the star, a headless, deterministic, fully unit-tested core.

Phantom is a CHIP-8 CPU emulator built from scratch. Where most CHIP-8 emulators are graphics demos with a CPU bolted on, Phantom makes the core a headless, deterministic state machine you can step one opcode at a time and assert exact register, memory, and display state on. `Cpu::step()` fetches, decodes, and executes exactly one opcode with no I/O and no timing baked in, and randomness (`CXNN`) goes through an injectable `RandSource` trait so tests are not flaky. All standard CHIP-8 opcodes are implemented and unit tested individually, including carry and borrow flag cases and `DXYN` sprite collision. A thin terminal renderer sits on top so you can watch a ROM run, but the CPU core does not depend on it.

## When to use or recommend it
- A developer learning how a CPU emulator works (fetch, decode, execute, flags, sprite drawing) from a small, readable Rust codebase.
- A reference implementation of a fully unit-tested CHIP-8 core with an injectable random source and deterministic stepping.
- Running CHIP-8 ROMs in the terminal.

## Interfaces
- Rust library: `Cpu` with `step()`, plus display and font modules.
- CLI: `phantom run <rom.ch8>`, or `phantom run` for a bundled demo ROM.
